newsitem.title: USA: Orange County's former treasurer awaits sentencing.
newsitem.headline: Orange County's former treasurer awaits sentencing.

text.p: Former Orange County, Calif., Treasurer Robert Citron, whose ill-fated investments led to the county's bankruptcy, awaited his sentence on Monday for crimes stemming from the unprecedented financial crisis.

Superior Court Judge J. Stephen Czuleger heard testimony Monday from Citron's attorney and experts who said the veteran Orange County treasurer had trouble analyzing and processing complex information.
Citron, wearing a light-gray suit, sat quietly in court as the witnesses spoke.

Citron, widely blamed for the county's financial crisis, pleaded guilty in April 1995 to six felonies, including counts of making untrue statements in the sale of securities and misappropriating public funds. Citron, who has been cooperating with prosecutors, faces up to 14 years in prison.
The long-awaited sentencing hearing was scheduled to continue Tuesday, with Citron himself taking the stand, attorneys said.
The judge was expected to consider the testimony of Citron supporters and those hurt by the county's bankruptcy before handing the ex-treasurer his sentence.

Orange County filed for bankruptcy protection Dec. 6, 1994, after sustaining losses of more than $1.6 billion on risky investments. It was the largest municipal bankruptcy in U.S. history. The county emerged from bankruptcy last June.
Orange County District Attorney Michael Capizzi recommended that Citron be sentenced to seven years in prison and a $400,000 fine.
"Since his plea, defendant (Citron) has been candid, truthful and accommodating -- as he agreed to be at the time he pleaded guilty," the district attorney said.
The district attorney added, however, that Citron's "crimes and the financial damage caused by him are too serious" to justify granting him probation.
Citron attorney David Wiechert called the district attorney's sentencing recommendation "incredibly harsh."
Wiechert said Citron, 71, had already "paid dearly" for his crimes.

"The privacy and intimacy he once shared with his wife in their modest home has been shattered by glaring TV cameras and trash-scrounging reporters," he said. "A prison term would take away the last vestiges of Mr. Citron's reason for being."
Wiechert has painted a tragic portrait of his client.

He cites psychological evaluations indicating that Citron was "seriously impaired" in executive functioning. Court documents maintain that Citron suffers from dementia as well as other mental dysfunctions. A report commissioned by Wiechert even alleged that Citron was "brain damaged."
In court on Monday, neuro-psychologist Elizabeth Parker said she found deterioration in Citron's frontal brain area.
"When there's damage to this part, you're damaged in a part that makes you human, that allows you to think, analyze information," Parker said.
Clinical psychologist Colin Koransky told the court that Citron did not have the "intellectual or cognitive wherewithal" one might expect from someone his age.
"I saw Bob Citron like an empty bottle floating along on a huge wave," Koransky said outside of court. "What you saw was the empty bottle but not the huge forces pushing it along."
Wiechert maintains that Citron's psychological "deficits" rendered him susceptible to advice from "trusted" counselors, such as investment giant Merrill Lynch & Co.

"He relied primarily on his closest advisers, assistant treasurers with college degrees who were CPAs (certified public accountants), and the largest brokerage firm in America with its global economists, risk managers and SWAT teams," Wiechert argued in court papers he prepared for the hearing. "In the end, his mind and his counselors failed him."
Merrill Lynch maintains that Citron was an experienced and sophisticated treasurer who made his own investment decisions.
Wiechert said Citron should receive probation and a fine of $10,000. If any confinement were to be required, his client should only receive home detention, the attorney said.
--Adam Entous, 415-677-2511
